newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen bull run meets US fund sales head-on.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen bull run meets US fund sales head-on.

text.p: The bull run of the key March Euroyen futures contract which was inspired by the steep decline in yen interest rate swaps was cut short by a large amount of selling by U.S. speculative funds by late morning trade on Friday.
The March rose as high as 99.03, but failed to go higher due to sales of 2,000 contracts by U.S. hedge funds at 99.02. It was at 99.02 at 0205 GMT, up sharply from Thursday's 98.97.
A long-term bank bought five- and seven-year fixed interest rates, a major city bank bought three-year and a major trust bank bought five-year swaps.
The three year IRS rate was quoted at 1.37/41 percent, down from 1.44/48 percent on Thursday.

"The sudden fall in the swap rates prompted a round of short-squeezing in the Euroyen market by traders who were wary of carrying their short positions over to the next week," said a city bank trader.
The Bank of Japan drained some 100 billion yen from the money market through its regular morning operation, leaving the market with a surplus of around 186 billion yen, traders said.
